text:
alex: quick design check — thinking about a simpler path for midstream failures: if a circuit-breaker trips while we're streaming, abandon the lease and fall back to a buffered non-streaming response instead of trying to resume. keeps edge stateless-ish and avoids lease transfer complexity. thoughts?

maria: curious: you mean tear down the streaming socket immediately and serve a full response from next backend call? that will increase p99 latency for those requests, right? :thinking_face: 

alex: yeah. tradeoff is increased latency for degraded requests vs complexity and correctness of transfer/lease logic. idea is to only do this for non-critical customers or requests tagged as "best-effort". for tiered customers we keep current resume/lease flow.

chao: two quick questions — 1) how do we avoid double side-effects if the original request reached the model and produced partial tokens? 2) billing implications if we re-run backend?

alex: good call. for side-effects we require idempotency tokens for any request that can mutate upstream (calls to tools/db). if not present, we default to fail-open w/ non-stream fallback that returns an error page. billing: count only final successful generation; if we re-run we attribute to fallback attempt and mark as degraded in telemetry so finance can decide.

maria: sgtm. can we make the policy pluggable per-route? e.g. in the route config:
```json
{"degrade_policy": "fallback_nonstream", "threshold": 0.2, "tiers": ["free","standard"]}
```

alex: exactly — route-level, plus a global kill-switch. also expose a metric: ingress.degraded_fallbacks{route,tier} and a synthetic p50/p95 of the fallback path.

liz: small UX nit — if we abort stream and then do non-stream, user sees nothing for longer. Can we emit a final SSE chunk that says "degraded" before closing so clients can show a clear banner?

achao: implementation-wise: edge should do these steps on circuit trip: 1) emit degradation trailer/event 2) close proxied stream 3) issue backend non-stream call with same idempotency token 4) stream final payload as single chunk (or 204 if backend refuses). playing that out with current proxy code is doable.

alex: pasted rough pseudo:
```bash
# on circuit trip
emit_event(client_conn, "X-DEGRADE:nonstream")
close_upstream_stream(upstream)
resp = call_backend_nonstream(req.copy_with({"idempotency": req.id}))
write_single_chunk(client_conn, resp.body)
```

maria: are we confident this won't break streaming consumer guarantees? i.e., some clients rely on partial tokens to show incremental UX. this change loses that. we should A/B it first.

alex: yes A/B. default to keep streaming for enterprise routes. also instrument client-visible indicators so FE teams can adapt.

liz: question: how to handle KV cache? if we resume vs rerun, token positions differ. if fallback reruns we should bypass prefix-KV and treat as fresh generation. document this.

achao: +1. implementation detail: set a header X-Edge-Fallback: rerun-no-kv to prevent accidental cache hits. also add tracing span that records "fallback_reason" and whether kv_bypassed=true.

sre-bot: deploy-checklist: update edge-proxy 0.53 config schema, add feature flag ingress.fallback_nonstream, add metrics, add integration test that simulates midstream ABORT and validates single-chunk response.

maria: integration test should assert telemetry: fallback_count increments and no double-billing tag. also stress-test with many concurrent fallbacks to see SLO impact.

alex: long-term: still want a resumable transfer protocol, but it's complex (multi-hop, lease handoff, KVS of trailing tokens). this fallback buys us time and reduces incidents.

liz: can we include a small compatibility shim in SDKs that detects X-DEGRADE and shows a friendly message so product doesn't feel broken?

alex: yes — add note in SDKs and docs under "Edge degradation modes". also include an example snippet for client:
```js
fetchStream(url).on('meta', m => { if (m.degrade) showBanner('Response degraded to non-stream') })
```

chao: anything else re: observability? we need to make degraded requests searchable by original request id and have a tie to lease attempts so debugging is easy.

alex: add enrichment: fallback_trace_id that references upstream lease attempts. log it at INFO level when fallback happens.

maria: ok i'm +1 for canarying this. i'll write a short RFC note for the rollout plan and highlight customer tiers, telemetry, and SDK compatibility.

alex: thanks — i'll start a small PR with the edge-proxy changes and the deploy-checklist from sre-bot. tagging @liz for SDK docs once we have signal. :thumbsup: 

liz: ack. i'll prep a short UX pattern for degraded streaming so PD knows what to surface.

sre-bot: reminder: please add integration tests to the PR and update the feature-flag gate in the staging config.

alex: timeline: aim for canary in staging by EOD next Tue, monitor fallback rate and client error spikes for 48h.

chao: nit: please include a concise diagram in the RFC that contrasts resume-vs-fallback flow — helps for oncall.

alex: will do. thanks all.
